suggestions.rationale: Prospective community studies support a temporal association in which social anxiety disorder can precede and is associated with increased subsequent risk of depressive disorders. This supports focused research only when a separately diagnosed social anxiety disorder predates a separately diagnosed depressive disorder. The studies establish population-level temporal risk, not proof of individual causation or aggravation, and require review of psychiatric chronology, diagnostic overlap, treatment, substance use, psychosocial stressors, and other competing contributors.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of social anxiety disorder diagnosis and onset
Independent documentation of depressive disorder diagnosis and onset
Chronology showing social anxiety disorder predating depressive disorder when a secondary theory is explored
Assessment of pre-existing depression, PTSD, generalized anxiety, other psychiatric illness, substance use, medication effects, and major psychosocial contributors
Qualified assessment distinguishing population-level temporal association from individual causation or aggravation

sourceReferences.citation: Stein MB, Fuetsch M, Müller N, Höfler M, Lieb R, Wittchen HU. Social anxiety disorder and the risk of depression: a prospective community study of adolescents and young adults. Arch Gen Psychiatry. 2001;58(3):251-256. doi:10.1001/archpsyc.58.3.251. PMID 11231832
sourceReferences.note: Prospective longitudinal community study. Among participants without depression at baseline, social anxiety disorder was associated with later depressive-disorder onset (OR 3.5, 95% CI 2.0-6.0). Supports temporal-risk research, not automatic individual causation.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 11231832; abstract Methods/Results: prospective longitudinal adolescent/young-adult community study; baseline SAD in nondepressed participants associated with depressive-disorder onset at follow-up, OR 3.5 (95% CI 2.0-6.0)

sourceReferences.citation: Beesdo K, Bittner A, Pine DS, et al. Incidence of social anxiety disorder and the consistent risk for secondary depression in the first three decades of life. Arch Gen Psychiatry. 2007;64(8):903-912. doi:10.1001/archpsyc.64.8.903. PMID 17679635
sourceReferences.note: Ten-year prospective longitudinal community/family study of 3,021 people. Social anxiety disorder was consistently associated with subsequent depression, reported RR range 1.49-1.85 after age/sex control. Supports temporal association, not an individual causal nexus by itself.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 17679635; abstract Design/Participants/Results: 10-year prospective longitudinal study; 3,021 participants; SAD consistently associated with subsequent depression, RR 1.49-1.85 controlling for age and sex
